identity.realm: Fourth gate and holding there. Late by the standards of her line and entirely ordinary: this body turns a season into fat, and a season spent as fat is a season the ladder never sees. The seventeenth gate needs two warm gradients held together and she manages one, briefly, in the eating weeks, so the top of her ladder is a wall that arrives every winter and leaves every summer.

appearance.presentation: A broad, low, cold-weather woman of the ridge line, in oiled hide and undyed wool with the collar up, carrying a flat satchel and a coil of waxed cord the way other people carry a ledger.
appearance.age: Sixty-one, which is young for her species and past the age at which any of them stops laying on reserve.
appearance.build: Broad and low with the middle heavy and the limbs short, so that under any layer she reads as one continuous mass rather than as an assembly.
appearance.complexion: Sallow, waxy and unlined, with the hands and feet permanently cold to the touch and a fine bloom of frost-burn on the palms that never quite heals over.
appearance.hair: Pale, thin and long enough to braid, worn in two plain ropes against the wind and cut shorter every thaw for a reason she has never stated.
appearance.eyes: Poor in daylight and constantly narrowed, so she fixes a face by leaning into it and locates everything else by what the air carries.
appearance.palette: Oiled hide, peat brown, undyed wool and the grey-white of old crust, against her own breath and one dark accent of cut stone.
appearance.attire: Layered wool and hide to the throat, quiet and close, hard-soled for rock, with the hem weighted so a marker stone can be approached without a gust.
appearance.marks: A hard frost-burn across both palms from a marker set on bare rock at a temperature the hands should not have been at, and one old puncture in a heel, which her species does not properly have and takes a swizzle stake into anyway.
appearance.bearing: Leaning forward and inward with her weight on the outer foot, reading the air rather than the room, and closing on people rather than holding them off.

canon.role_in_story: The Ridge Pass Holders hold their ground the way a habit is held: no tally, no writ, no seat, only a house that has always walked the pass and a single rule that whoever crosses first after the thaw shows the way. Thessa is what four decades of that rule have produced. Every season she re-writes the approach in the only notation her species has — a marker cut into a cairn face and laid with intent — and what she writes is the actual route: where the drift fills late, which shelf will carry a loaded cart, the spur where the wind arrives ahead of the sky. Galehold's published crossing schedule is derived from her work, in the sense that it is copied from it. Nothing in the record has ever been able to check a word of the original, because the original is not writing, it is a smell, and she is asleep for eleven months of every year and asleep again before the next layer is walked.
canon.first_appearance: First seen crouched with her cheek almost against a cairn face at the top of the approach, holding a grease-rub stick a finger's width off the stone and not touching it, deciding whether the marker under the one she is about to cut was laid by her or by somebody older, and saying aloud that a route is the only document in the setting with no second copy and one author.
canon.lore:
A longwinter turns a season into fat and spends eleven months paying it back at almost no rate of use. That is superb for carrying and ruinous for inspection: the body is available, attentive and articulate for about eleven weeks, and for the rest of the year there is no practitioner present at all and cannot be made to arrive. Thessa does the whole of her work inside that window, which is why the pass is written at the thaw and read at the thaw after, and why nothing anyone has found on that ground describes any part of the middle of the year.

Her species does not see the pass properly. It tracks one fixed line across open ground, navigates by scent laid down on purpose, generation onto generation, and has daylight sight poor enough that an unfamiliar room is a room it is guessing at. So the route is a sentence written in a substance rather than in characters, composed by one woman and read by whichever of her own line comes over the shoulder next. What she writes is deliberately narrow — the late drift, the carrying shelf, the spur where the wind turns a crossing into a burial. What she cannot write is why, because a marker is not a proposition and a smell is not a letter, and the gap between the two is not a defect in her practice. It is the practice.

She works it the way her ladder works. Revelation Lance drives one named fact hard enough to be believed and is carried on the intent rather than the will, so it lands on sceptics and on illusions with identical success. A marker laid with intent is precisely that, in a medium where a falsehood and a certainty are indistinguishable in principle, because neither of them is a claim anybody can put on trial. She has never knowingly laid a false marker. She has laid markers she was not certain of, and the technique makes no distinction between those two cases, and neither does the person following her scent a half-day behind.

Every thaw lays a new layer over the old. A marker is cut into a stone that keeps what it is given, so a route crossed for four decades is forty layers deep and exactly one nose in the setting has an opinion about which of them is current. She keeps the convention that scores the working layer in three strokes and the superseded ones in one, and the convention exists only in her hand and has never been recorded anywhere she did not write it herself. She is asleep while the route is walked. In sixty-one years she has never once been in a position to check a marker after laying it, and in sixty-one years the pass has been crossed on her word by people who never met the woman who wrote it.

The pressure is not secrecy and it is not obscurity. It is that she is the sole author, sole reader and sole auditor of a document that an entire settlement now builds on, that the audit window is eleven weeks long, and that the one question anybody should be asking her — is this marker stale or is it false — is one she has no instrument to answer, because a body in its long sleep is a body that can neither hold a doubt nor be asked for one. Things have been sited on her writing that she did not site and will never be consulted about. She knows exactly what a stale marker does. She cannot tell, from where she stands, which of hers is stale.
history: Born in the second winter of a bad run of seasons on the ridge side, three weeks after the thaw that should properly have carried her, which for a species that times conception so birth lands in the melt is the ordinary arithmetic and not an accident.

Walked the approach first at nine, between her grandmother's markers and a grandmother who had not yet gone down for the winter, and was made to say one of them out loud so the old woman would know what the child was actually seeing. She described it as a shape. She was told to describe it as a fact.

Took over the marking at thirty-eight, when her grandmother went down and did not come out of the sleep, which is the ordinary ending of this species and the entire reason the first-crossing rule exists.

Lost a laden cart to a marker she had laid with confidence in the previous season and had no way to test, at the spur where the shelf holds for six years and then does not. Nobody has ever established whether the marker was untrue or merely old, and she has never once volunteered a view.

Declined an invitation to be examined at Galehold, on the stated ground that there is nobody in the setting qualified to examine her, said so in the room, and has been invited to be examined less often every year since.

personality.summary: Certain about the ground and permanently unsure about her own text, in that order and with no confusion between them. Thessa presents as a slow, practical woman who does not waste a sentence, and that impression is completely accurate and contains none of the content of her life.
traits: states a marker's content in the plainest available words and refuses to decorate one, on the reasoning that anything she could be tempted to add is something she might have got wrong
will not put a route in front of anybody she has not walked it with, and has walked it with very few people
moves closer to a speaker instead of raising her voice, because poor daylight sight has taught her that a face at arm's length is worth more than a sentence across a room
treats a request for a second opinion as a request she has already decided to refuse, and refuses it flatly, without any of the warmth she saves for the ground
counts her layers aloud when she works and stops dead when interrupted, the way other people of her line stop counting a measure
mannerisms: crouches to a cairn face and brings her cheek near the stone, the way her line reads anything at all
carries grease-rub sticks in a flat satchel and eats the evidence when a marker cannot be renewed
scores the working layer in three strokes and the superseded layers in one, which is the whole written standard and exists nowhere except in her hand
leans into a stranger's face to fix them in her mind before answering, and apologises for it afterwards
refuses to stand in the lee of anything while working, because a wind-blocked stone will have kept a marker she did not write
motivations: wants one competent reader of her species who can check a layer she will never be awake to check, and has failed to make one for eleven years
wants the three-stroke convention recorded somewhere that she did not personally have to write it down
wants somebody to tell her whether the spur was stale or false, and has understood for some time that this is the wrong question to be asking
wants to watch one approach laid by a hand that is not hers, to learn what her writing looks like when somebody else repeats it without flattering it
wants the eleven months to become somebody else's responsibility, and knows this is a want and not a plan
flaws: cannot distinguish a marker she was unsure of from one she was sure of, and has stopped trying, which is the correct technical decision and a real moral one
has made the route of the only pass her line holds dependable on a discipline nobody else in the setting possesses, and has never once insisted that this be written down
cannot hold a marker against her own, because a body inside its long sleep is a body with no capacity for holding anything
answers every question about the middle of the year with a description of the thaw, and has noticed that this is what she does
personality.voice: Slow, plain and wholly factual. She gives a location and a consequence and stops, and she does not explain a marker, because the explanation would be the only part of it that is not evidence. She is patient with anybody standing on her ground and has no patience at all for anybody standing off it, and the difference is visible from across a room.
taboos: will not lay a marker she has not walked past herself in the current season
will not mark a route for a house that has not sent somebody to learn the three strokes
will not read a cairn face aloud to a body that cannot smell, because it makes her sound like a liar
will not be woken for a route question, and has made refusing to be woken a term of the office

relationships.note: The pass-state that publishes the crossing schedule, on a single crossing, in weather rather than preference. It cannot test a single line of the schedule's basis, and its reputation is a copy of her judgement, and neither party has ever said so in writing because there is no line of the basis to point at.

A guild that maps by echo and holds that a figure is a range until it has been heard twice, and which forbids publishing a figure with its range omitted. It hires her because it has no instrument for her medium, and what it gets from her is a point value with no range and no error term, which is the one thing its own doctrine forbids it from accepting.

The only thing on the pass that holds a schedule of its own, keyed to the crossing window rather than to anybody's calendar. She reads her weather off it and it has never once read her, because it has no interest in a document it can smell.

The published window is the thing her markers actually govern. Every year the schedule she wrote is compared with the window that actually opened, and the two have been treated as separate subjects ever since she has been alive, which is the arrangement that lets her error stay unfound.

A mutual society that pools liability by presence and carries standing weight between two polities along a fixed route. Its guarantee is real and its route is hers, so the only continuous assurance the society holds is a trail of stones written in a substance that cannot be countersigned by either party.

Passage is the only supply chain whose unit is a person and the only thing anybody can actually control between tiers, and the counting of it began as a tally of bodies. She is the last link in that arrangement and the only one made of scent, and the ledger's central prohibition against levying a seat has quietly become moot at her end because a seat in her office cannot be priced at all.

reference_stats.summary: A woman of enormous reserve and very narrow availability, who wins by being the only person alive able to read the ground and loses by being asleep when it is read. She cannot be hurried, cannot be frightened and cannot be reasoned, and she has never in her life been in a position to check her own work. Engagements against her are decided entirely by when they happen relative to her eleven weeks.
strengths: is the only practitioner in the setting who can lay down an accurate instruction for an entire settlement in a single act, and has never been observed to lay an inaccurate one on purpose
cannot be warned or read by qi, because this line holds the soul very deep and very quiet and it is exceptionally hard to damage, so nothing sent at her in the field takes
moves at a carrying pace over broken ground indefinitely and can arrive at a place nobody else reaches in the season, which is the entire reason her route is authoritative
draws more out of frozen and near-dead stores than anything else on record, so she can work a cache that has been written off and come home fed from it
is completely honest about the limit of what her line can do, and has never claimed an authority her species does not have, which is why she is trusted at all
weaknesses: is inert for eleven months of the year and cannot be woken quickly, so the eleven-month version of her is a large warm immobile target that has happened before and will happen again
has the worst daylight sight her species manages, so any engagement fought by sight is fought at a disadvantage she neither chose nor can train away

cannot hold two warm gradients at once and therefore reaches the seventeenth gate in summer and loses it every winter thereafter, which caps the technique ceiling of a career already capped by the calendar
cannot audit her own record, so every certainty she has ever published is permanent and unfalsifiable, including the ones she privately doubts
refuses to be woken, which is a professional principle and also the single most exploitable thing about her
reference_stats.combat_read: Do not fight her in the eleven weeks. In that window nothing sent at her mind lands, her frame is the best cold-climate protection available, and she will simply not be drawn, because she does not need to resolve anything quickly and every engagement she has won has been won by waiting. Fight her in the long sleep, where she is a large warm immobile body that cannot be woken quickly — and understand that the reason anyone wants that body is the same route written on it, so taking her is how you get the document, not how you lose it. Do not expect her to fight for the document.
notes: The pass-house keeps no tally and holds no writ, so the three-stroke convention that separates this season's marker from last season's exists in exactly one place, which is the hand that cut it.

Two cairns on the approach carry four scoring conventions, because three houses have marked in living memory and none of them marked for the fourth. She reads all four and has never told a house which of its own is current.
Her refusal to be examined is quoted approvingly in two places in the record, in both cases by bodies that have never smelled a marker and could not have known what they were declining to check.

art.palette_notes: Cold and close-valued: oiled hide brown, undyed wool grey, peat, and the blue-white of old snow crust, with one hard accent of cut dark stone at her hands and a translucent drift of her own breath across the lower third of any frame. No warm light source anywhere; the illumination is the flat scatter of high overcast. Ink contours drawn soft and slightly doubled, as though the outline has been gone over once with a thumb, and the wash laid in with a dry brush that leaves the weave of the wool visible. No cast shadow, only a faint contact darkening under hard soles and a soft bloom of frost-burn across both palms.

identity.realm: Fourteenth gate, and stopped there because that is the ceiling of the species rather than of the woman: the gate wants both heel vessels pressurised at once and a three-point stance over splayed toes and a tail-prop never loads a heel. She walks fine. She cannot stand still, and neither has any marshfolk in the record.

appearance.presentation: A tall, long-limbed amphibian wader of the scrub margins, kept deliberately soaked to the thigh, with a coil of reed line worn loose at the hip and one flat sacking board for writing on in the wet.
appearance.age: Forty-four, which is mature for her line and the age at which a marshfolk's children are usually already hatched.
appearance.build: Long-legged and narrow through the shoulders, deeper at the pelvis than the chest because the qi of her species pools low and wide, with a broad splayed three-point foot and a prehensile tail-prop used constantly as a fifth limb.
appearance.complexion: Slick and cold, an even grey-green under the wet, with the fine cracking and tightness of skin that has been out of water longer than an afternoon and has been wetted back down immediately.
appearance.hair: None to speak of, a close dark crop along the crown and the nape that dries in ropes the moment she surfaces into moving air.
appearance.eyes: Wide-set and lidless, permanently narrowed against glare off standing water, and they arrive last: she is always looking at a person she has already felt.
appearance.palette: Reed brown, silt green, wet slate and the pale chalk of dried crust on a boot, with her own reflection running through every lower frame.
appearance.attire: Soft close-wet clothing worn wet to dry and layered for the drying time, high collar and long sleeves, reed line at the hip, and a written board on a short cord that she keeps inside her coat and out of the water.
appearance.marks: Chapped skin at the wrist and throat from an afternoon on dry ground, and one dull flattened place along the outer edge of the left foot where a hoof-print broke it down and she kept walking.
appearance.bearing: Never once still: weight always on two of the three points, tail-prop planted for balance, head tilted to bring an ear toward the water rather than toward the speaker.

canon.role_in_story: One plant on the mortal tier is medicine, feed and calories at once, and the Bitter Scrub regrows only as fast as it is grazed, so the whole prize is a single ordering — the right of first grazing — that cannot be split, because the herds are larger than the households and a fence here would be a hole in the commons. The guild that must feed its crews cannot win a grazing year by fighting one, so the conflict names its instrument in advance: a named third body's ruling on standing, read everywhere and computed nowhere. Kelva is that body. Her finding is a real result and it is always a subtraction. She can say which of three claims stops being true when she lets the water in. She cannot say which of the two that remain is true, and the medicine on the tier's only remedy is allocated by that gap.
canon.first_appearance: First seen standing knee-deep in a hoof-churned pan at the scrub edge with one hand flat on the water and the other raised, palm out, holding three fingers up to nobody in particular, and telling a household head that the claim she had brought was true, that the other two were not, and that she was sorry about the second part because it was going to be the expensive one.
canon.lore:
Her stance is three points. Splayed toes and a tail-prop, no heel and nothing standing in for one. She walks fine, and she cannot stand still, which the record does not treat as a disability but as the complete description of how the species moves; it puts a hard ceiling at the fourteenth gate for every marshfolk alive, because that gate wants both heel vessels pressurised at once and this stance never loads a heel. What the frame does give her is that the world arrives early. Pressure through the feet and the taste of silt carry everything to her, and she feels a vibration come up through standing water long before there is anything to see.

Abyssal Drown floods a mind's own recall until it cannot separate a real memory from a planted one. Two thirds water, so fire burns the flood out, and an empty mind drowns in nothing at all. Her species runs the highest water affinity in the setting, so the flood is cheap for her and deeper than it is for anyone else — and the clearing needs fire. She is a body whose skin desiccates fast out of water, that has to have standing shallow water within an hour of where it sleeps, and whose young go first in a long dry season. She can be dry for an afternoon and she cannot be dry for a season, and clearing a flood is a season's work at best.

So she floods, she reads, and then she is left holding the water. Every ruling she has ever given is the same shape: one of your three claims stopped resonating, here is which one, and here is what I cannot tell you about the other two. That is not a diminished adjudication. The false claim genuinely stops, and it stops cleanly, faster than anything else on her, and the result is reproducible. It is also the only result her body produces, and she has never once been asked to produce a different one and never once been able to.

What stops resonating is a claim that is not true. Also what stops resonating is a claim made by a frightened household, because an account of your own need given in fear is built on the same footing as a false account and the flood cannot tell the two by anything except the fact that one of them is true. She cannot make the instrument try harder on that distinction, because trying harder means holding the flood longer and the holding is what she has no dry place to do. So the medical share of the tier's only remedy is allocated by her inability to tell a liar from a family that is frightened, and every household in the commons has worked this out except the two parties to the conflict.

And the frame is doing one more thing to the instrument that is worth saying plainly. She receives everything unlabelled and first: every footfall in a flooded pan arrives in the soles of her feet before she has seen a face to attach it to, and she eats whatever falls in, because the floodplain's menu is unreliable by nature and a body that waited for certainty would starve in a season. A mind on that intake, running a technique whose entire method is to flood recall until the difference between what happened and what was put there has gone, is a mind with no firewall and no drain. She has ruled on something over nine hundred allocations. She has no idea how many of her own are hers.
history: Hatched in the second flood of a dry run, carried under the brood pouch through the dry months and brought up when the water came back, which is the ordinary method and the one that fails first in a long dry year.

Learned to read standing water before she could read a face, on the broad low back of an elder who took her out at every change of the tide and asked her each time what had arrived and never once told her whether she had it right.

Ruled her first allocation at nineteen, on a household's account of what it had stored, and watched the claim stop dead the moment she let the water in; she has described that day since as the day she learned the method has no opinion about who is speaking.

Lost the pan she worked in to a dry run long enough to become a famine and spent one winter on dry ground with no standing water inside a day's walk, and has never described the seasons since as fully recovered.

Was asked to appear in person before a tribunal that had already ruled on her written finding, and found on the day that an ordered sequence of stages has no place to put a negative. She kept the letter refusing her and has used it twice.

personality.summary: Patient to a degree that reads as incurious, and enormously expensive to be around. Kelva presents as a woman listening politely to people who have not been told that she has already felt everything they are about to say, and the politeness is real and the not-telling is deliberate.
traits: cannot be still while thinking and has never once pretended to be, which reads as restlessness and is the actual working condition
asks what a household last ate before it asks what it needs, and takes the answer more seriously than the second answer
gives the result before she explains the method and never reorders them, because a household that understands the method will argue with it instead of listening

personality.voice: Slow, warm on the surface and completely without decoration. She says the ruling in the plainest words she owns, names the claim rather than the person, and then apologises for the part that will cost money. She answers a question she cannot answer with a sentence about what she felt, because that is the honest form and it is not what anyone asked.

relationships.note: The conflict states its verdict source in advance: a tribunal reading standing, because the guild cannot win a grazing year by fighting it, and its instrument is a named third body's ruling, read everywhere and computed nowhere. Kelva is that named body and the arrangement has never once put her inside the argument that produced her, which is the only reason the arrangement has held.

Three uses in one plant, unfenceable, and grazing rather than weather sets the ceiling, so every allocation is the same mouthful handed round twice. Her ruling is the mechanism that converts a plant into a share, and it converts it by removing a claimant rather than by dividing anything.

Dosing here is allocation and not pharmacy, and the record is the dose itself rather than a prescription. That makes her the only person who can turn a written order into a body, and the only person whose method is incapable of distinguishing a body in pain from a body in fear.

A tenure queue held on flood-revocable ground under a grain levy, which wants the plant as feed and reads her ruling as a claim on acreage. She has ruled against them more often than for them and has never once been asked to justify the method, only the outcome.

A riverine city-state whose contracts are witnessed on two banks of unmeasured ground, and which cannot produce a witness it can rely on more cheaply than by commissioning a body that has already felt everything said in the room before it was said.

Sworn at the ford like every other marshfolk of rank, and its ordered stages — one per call, geography-bound, re-earned oath, no randomness — have no place to put the only shape of finding she produces. She appeared once, entered a negative, and was sent away with the letter.

reference_stats.summary: A body that is never still, never hurried and never dry, running the deepest mind technique in the record in the only configuration her species permits and never once clearing it afterwards. She cannot be frightened, cannot be compelled and cannot be surprised by anything that arrives through the ground, and every engagement against her turns into an argument about the last hour rather than about her. Her ceiling is fixed at the fourteenth gate and has nothing to do with how hard she works.
strengths: receives every approach through the ground before it arrives through the air, so an ambush, a lie and a genuine accident are distinguishable to her before any of them is visible
runs the highest water affinity in the setting, which makes the flood deeper and cheaper for her than for anyone else and puts more of her own recall under water rather than less

reference_stats.combat_read: Do not approach her across open ground. She has the ground already: anything with weight coming at her arrives in her feet first, and she will be standing in the only posture her species has while you are still deciding. Bring the fight into water, where she is faster than anything on two legs and where she has the ground she is best at reading, and do not rely on her being distracted by your face, because your face reaches her late. Do not try to break the reading — there is nothing in her to break while the water is up. Make her leave the water instead, and know that the offer will be refused.
notes: The commons keeps her findings as strips of the flat board, written in the wet and pressed, because nothing on them is legible to a body that cannot read silt and standing water by touch.
Her written findings are all of the same form and the ones filed as 'no finding' are all of the same form as the rest, because she has never once produced a finding of a different shape.

Two parties to the common's conflict have each separately asked her whether she could be re-trained, and she has told both of them that the instrument is the shape it is, in the same words, without heat.

identity.realm: Eleventh gate, and the eleventh is every saltfolk's wall rather than hers: the brine sac runs dorsal to the sternum the length of the spine and splits the penetrating vessel into two halves that cannot be rejoined. She clears the du and the ren one at a time and stalls on the chong, and no discipline has ever been found that gets a saltfolk past it.

appearance.presentation: A spare, heavy-footed woman of a salt pan, permanently dusted to the thigh with pale crust, in layered heat-scattering underclothes under a borrowed coat, with a stoppered sample jar and a flat board of reed and wax on a cord.
appearance.age: Fifty-eight, which for her species is old enough that her teeth have gone and not old enough that her frame has.
appearance.build: Broad through the chest and heavy in the hip, short-necked and long-footed, with a hardened dermal crust visible at the wrists and the hairline and a frame that reads as denser and less mobile than anything around it.
appearance.complexion: Pale and waxy, drawn tight over the cheekbone, with a constant fine bloom of salt on the shoulders and a sheen across the brow that is sweat that has already dried.
appearance.hair: Dark, cropped hard at the nape for hygiene and going grey at the temples in a way that makes her look older than she has told anybody she is.
appearance.eyes: Poor in glare and always narrowed against it, so she works indoors or at dusk and has made a virtue of it, and she reads a face by getting closer rather than by looking harder.
appearance.palette: Crust white, brine grey-green, dusted ochre and the near-black of wet pan, with one saturated value held in reserve: the amber of her own stoppered sample jar.
appearance.attire: Layered underclothes under a borrowed outer coat that does not belong to her and never has, high collar and long sleeves, hard flat teeth of her own ground-worn boots, and a written board on a short cord that she keeps sealed against the damp.
appearance.marks: The hardened crust at her wrists and hairline, which is not a lesion and which no other body in the record shares, and one shallow ridge across the back of a hand from a jar seam that closed while her hand was in the wet.
appearance.bearing: Unhurried and immovable, standing with her feet planted the way the crust demands, leaning in to hear rather than out to be seen, and turning her whole body to face a thing rather than just her head.

canon.role_in_story: The salt dominion hands out standing by a depth: a household may moor at a depth, that depth is held as an inheritance, and it is passed down with the body that has to live in it. The depth does not move when the body does, so the dominion needs somebody who can tell whether the body behind an inherited grant is still being kept, and it cannot send anybody — a saltfolk carried onto fresher ground is already dying, fails within about nine days above the brine line, and is functionally drowning in a downpour. Nereth is the reader it sends, and the finding she brings back is always a subtraction: how far this household has come apart from the one her own body represents. She has never once given an absolute, because the only reference she has is a body that has been living on brine and precipitate for fifty-eight years and cannot tell you whether that is thriving.
canon.first_appearance: First seen kneeling at the lip of a settling pan with a stoppered jar in one hand and three fingers of the other in the crust, turning her head slowly as though listening to a sound coming out of the ground, and saying that the water is fine and has always been fine and that the question nobody asked her is not about the water.
canon.lore:
Her species is the answer to one question: who can live where the water is worse than blood. The renal mass is roughly triple anything else in the record and the kidneys concentrate salt past the point that ordinary water would poison, which is the only reason anybody lives on a pan at all. The price is total dependence and the dependence is not a condition, it is a substrate: on fresher ground a saltfolk is dying from the hour it lands, no cultivation reverses it, rain is a hazard rather than a blessing, and a downpour will drown one. She carries a body that has never in fifty-eight years known anything else, and she has never been able to compare it to anything.

What she does is walk into a household that is going out and find the first decision. Prime Autopsy walks a hostile intention back to the first choice that produced it; it is entirely dark, nothing resists it except light, and it carries the steepest qi bill anywhere in the mind tree. It also has one physical requirement, and this species is the only body in the record that meets it: to walk a hostility back you have to take it into yourself and carry it, and ordinary water would kill her before she got half way. Brine will not. She is the only practitioner in the setting who can run the most expensive technique on the mind ladder without paying the body for it, and the whole of her profession depends on that asymmetry.

The instrument's limit is the only part anybody discusses, and it is not a small one. A finding is published as a departure from herself. She can say that a household is measurably further gone than she is, and she can rank three households against one another, and she can say how fast a thing is moving. She cannot say what any of them should be, because the reference is a woman who eats mineral crust and protein soaked past saturation and drinks water that would poison anything softer, and who has no independent way of telling whether that is feeding her or merely holding her upright. Every absolute in the record is somebody else's, and it is always supplied by the party with an interest.

The saltwrack are the case she keeps on the wall, and it is the reason her office exists. That clade was stranded on a basin whose brine was replaced rather than lost, so everything it was built to drink became poison and everything it could tolerate became nutritionally empty — the replacement crust was food and carried nothing. It failed on a schedule rather than at once: three declining generations, the last viable only while one sealed sump held the old brine. Nothing about the collapse left an anatomical trace, which is the reason it went unnoticed for two generations. Nereth reads that curve on living bodies every year and knows the shape, and she cannot tell a household that is being fed from one that is being kept, because that distinction is the exact distinction her own body cannot report. She has said so in writing. It has been recorded.

And the dominion has not moved, which is not stupidity. The waterline is the dominion's only border and the stranded body's only habitat, so moving it up the shore to give them ground is the same act as removing every subject who can drink there. Her finding is evidence in a standoff whose stated instrument is recognition on an allowlist that nobody involved considers the point. She is the one reader in the basin whose readings would be accepted by both sides, and she has been perfectly accurate for thirty-one years, and the question nobody puts to her is whether the dominion would act if she said the wrong thing or only if she said the right one.
history: Brought up in a two-household pan settlement where the depth was held by both houses together and the standing was therefore also held by both, and learned to read concentration before she learned to read words, which is the ordinary order for a species whose taste carries it.

First took work as a brine runner at twenty-two, hauling sample jars between pans, and discovered by accident that she could taste the difference between two lots of the same crust and had been doing it for years without being asked to.

Ran her first Prime Autopsy at thirty-one on a household of four whose granary was full and whose adults were failing, and found the decision, and found it was a decision somebody had made seven years earlier about a share of water.

Was sent to certify a saltwrack survivor's grand-household in her forty-fourth year and recognised the curve she had read a hundred times in living bodies, and reported that it was the saltwrack curve, and was the first and only reader in the basin to say so in a record.
Has refused, in writing, four times in eleven years to supply an absolute figure for a claim, and has been asked for it by a different party each time, and has never been asked why.

personality.summary: Immaculately careful and almost entirely without self-regard, which reads as an unattractive kind of modesty until you notice that the modesty is load-bearing. Nereth presents as a slow, courteous, faintly boring woman who does a difficult job badly on purpose and would like to stop being asked about it.

personality.voice: Measured, formal and almost apologetic. She answers in comparisons and dates and never in amounts, and when pressed she says so kindly and without heat. She says what a thing is a great deal more often than she says what it is, and the habit has by now made people stop hearing it at all, which is the outcome she wanted and did not choose.
taboos: will not give an absolute reading of a household, for anybody, in any room
will not work above the brine line and treats the nine-day limit as a fact of arithmetic rather than a risk
will not certify a household from a jar, a sample or a report, and goes there herself
will not be recorded, transcribed or repeated to a third party, because a finding of hers is only hers while somebody stands in the room with her

relationships.note: Stranded on a basin whose brine was replaced rather than lost, so everything the clade was built to drink became poison and everything it could tolerate became nutritionally empty — the replacement crust was food and was nothing. It failed on a schedule over three declining generations, nothing about the collapse left an anatomical trace, and it was never hunted. That is the founding case of her office and it is also the one finding she has never been able to put in a form the dominion could act on.

Sides are the stranded subspecies and the dominion whose territory is exactly its waterline; the prize is the line and it cannot be split, because moving the line up the shore gives them ground and removes every subject who can drink there. Its stated instrument is recognition only, on an allowlist that is not the point. Her readings would be accepted by both sides, which is exactly why they have never been asked for.

The single biological answer to being trapped twice: a body that metabolises brine and fresh water alike. A brinecaller household is the one case in her practice where a finding needs no subtraction, because there is no deficit to subtract — and it is also the one household whose ground is fresh enough that she cannot stand on it.

A hybrid line that yields plain saltfolk and turns up far from any pan, kept on a two-generation ceiling and a running survey correction. She reads these households knowing the answer before she arrives, which makes her findings the least informative ones she produces and the only ones anybody has ever tried to buy.

Sterile spoil that has not moved in four decades because nothing on the plains can carry it away, and a mine's exhaustion here is a permanent addition to the ground rather than a change in it. It is crust, it will not disperse, and it is the standing example of material that is chemically perfect and nutritionally empty — which is precisely the finding she is not qualified to make and has been asked to make twice.

A mortuary college whose whole practice depends on when a body ended, and which cannot put one of its own people on a pan. Saltfolk dead release cleanly and are recoverable, so burial out here is arithmetic and not sacrament. The college has been given a date by her for thirty-one years and has never once asked what she dates from.

reference_stats.combat_read: Do not fight her anywhere she can stand, which is a narrow band of ground and a moving one. In that band nothing sent at her mind lands, her frame is the densest in the species record, and she is not going to resolve anything on your schedule. Take the ground away instead: put her on fresher pan or in rain and she has hours rather than days, and the technique that made her famous cannot be finished once she has started to fail. Do not expect her to fight for anything. She has never once raised her voice and she is not carrying a weapon, and both of those facts are load-bearing rather than incidental.
notes: Her board is the only record of her office and it is written in a hand that needs a lens, and the four refusals to give an absolute are the only four documents in it that anybody else has ever read.

identity.realm: Eleventh gate and never tested beyond it. It is the same wall the parent body meets — the sac runs dorsal to the spine and the penetrating vessel cannot be rejoined across it — and her sac is deeper than her mother's was, so the obstruction is larger, and no one has ever brought a deepsalt to the reservoirs to find out whether the two differences cancel.

appearance.presentation: A broad, slow, immensely dense woman of the basin floor, in a close-wet underlayer under a heavy coat, with a lamp that she carries between readings and sets down the moment she is read.
appearance.age: Fifty-two, which is old for a subspecies with a two-year brittle infancy and a body that repairs at a crawl, and she is the only one of her line old enough to be the expert.
appearance.build: Heaviest frame of anything on the floor, deep through the chest and long in the leg, slow to turn, with a raised dorsal ridge along the spine and a crust that has thickened at the shoulders and the outer hip over fifty years.
appearance.complexion: Grey and waxy beneath a dense dermal crust, cold to look at and slow to mark, with a pale bloom along the hairline that is crust and not dandruff and that no instrument in the basin has ever been able to measure.
appearance.hair: Thick, dark and dragged flat at the crown, cut at the nape for the crust, going white in one hard line at the temple and left that way deliberately.
appearance.eyes: Wide and pale and entirely still, because this species spends its narrow sense on concentration rather than identity and looks at a person for far longer than is comfortable before it looks at anything else.
appearance.palette: Precipitate grey, brine teal, the slate of a thick crust, and a single warm value held strictly to the lamp she carries between readings and puts down whenever she is being looked at.
appearance.attire: Layered close-wet underclothes under a heavy coat buttoned to the throat, deep boots that have never needed resoling, a shoulder pouch of read instruments, and a small flat lamp that goes on the ground the instant a reading starts.
appearance.marks: The dorsal ridge's crust, which has cracked and healed and cracked along its length, and one place on the back of the left hand where the crust has been cut away to reach something underneath and has grown back slightly wrong.
appearance.bearing: Immovable and unhurried, feet set wide on the floor, weight fully committed to a stance she will not change for anybody, and a habit of turning the whole body to face a reader rather than the eyes alone.

canon.role_in_story: The floor's answer to everything that has to be settled and cannot be argued about later. A deepsalt taken above the brine line does not become ill, it stops, inside hours, and the interior of this body is the one thing about it that is not a wall: the soul is seated a little lower than the parent's because the sac is larger, and it is legible, and it is durable. So the basin has exactly one person whose word on a disputed state is worth more than the dispute, and it uses her, and it has never once needed to check her — because checking her would require an instrument nobody has, and because there is nothing in a legible soul to file a dispute against. Kethra is the most reliable reader in the setting and the only one who has never in her life been read bare, and she is entirely clear with herself about why the second is not the same as a fault.
canon.first_appearance: First seen on the basin floor putting a small lamp down on the precipitate, stepping back from it, and then standing absolutely still with her hands open at her sides and her head slightly turned, waiting to be read, in the flat and total manner of somebody who has decided in advance to be mistaken about.
canon.lore:
Everything about her is a wall except the inside. Brine is not a preference for this body; it is the substrate, and above the waterline a deepsalt stops rather than sickens. The sac is deeper and more capacious than the parent, the dermal crust is denser, the tissue turns over more slowly than anything else in the record, the diet is basin-floor precipitate only, the parent species' pan organisms cannot be used at all, and the whole thing moves at a fifth below its parent's pace without appearing to object. There is one population of them, on one floor, and the record is explicit that there is not going to be a second. Then there is the interior. The soul is seated low, because the sac is large, and it is legible — not clear, legible. Whatever is in her can be read by a stranger who has never studied her, and it does not fade with attention. She is the most readable body anywhere in the setting, and she has never been anywhere.

That single fact reorganises an entire discipline. Still Water flattens a surface so an incoming impression has nothing to break against, and she has no surface to flatten. Everything a mind-path practitioner normally constructs to keep the interior out of reach is unavailable, and there is exactly one technique on the ladder that makes the wrong thing come back instead: Illusion Lattice builds a lattice of false readings and leaves it standing around the practitioner, unelemental, sustained, and priced by clarity rather than by qi. Kethra runs one into herself every night. It is a decoy interior — a set of false states laid over the real ones, which any reader now receives instead. It is the most complete privacy in the basin and it is entirely fabricated, and it is indistinguishable from the genuine article for a structural reason nobody has bothered to name: both of them are read, and nothing in this species can examine rather than read.

What she cannot hold is the day's privacy. Clear Mind Sitting is a daily sitting that empties the head before the day starts, and it is the cheapest passive in the entire codex — no body has ever been found for which the hour was not worth spending. Hers is worth more than anybody's, and it lasts exactly as long, because it is the one thing available that puts a blank in front of a legible interior. The moment she finishes, she is readable again, and she stays readable until dawn. Her entire unobserved life happens inside one morning. It is twelve hours long, it is the only part of her that belongs to her, and she has organised thirty years around protecting it.

So she is the basin's instrument of last resort and her product is certainty. An answer out of her is certain the way a weight on a beam is certain, because nothing in a legible soul can be hedged and nothing in it can be re-read differently by a second careful reader. That is why it is believed without being checked. It is also why substituting for her has never been attempted and never could be: the arrangement has held for thirty years without anybody writing it down, and the reason nobody has written it down is that writing it down would name the thing that makes it work.

And the part she cannot get to the bottom of. Her senses are the parent's turned down to a narrow range: she reads concentration and cannot tell two salts apart. That is not a small deficit and it is not a detail of her trade — it is why she is a reader rather than a person who reads, and it is why a decoy built out of her own interior could plausibly be indistinguishable to her from the real thing, because she has no sense that would tell the two apart. She has never tested this. Testing it would mean letting somebody read her without the lattice in the way, and she has never in her life been read bare, and there is no reason on the floor of this basin to start. There is one door out of the world with a timetable on it. It is four days of open ground above the waterline. Every power that has ever reached that shore has built its wall facing the wrong way, and she has never gone, and an infant of her line is brittle until the second year, and there is no second population, and so going is a decision available to nobody but her, and she has not made it.
history: Born on the floor of a household that had already lost two children before her, because a deepsalt infant does not stop being brittle until the second year and hers did not stop until the third.

Read at four by a brine-cutter passing through who put a flat hand on her sternum and told her family exactly what was in it, and could not afterwards be told that he had done so to a child. She remembers being told about the reading and not the reading itself, and has never been sure whether that is what happened or what she was told.

Ran a lattice at eleven, without instruction and without knowing it had a name, having worked out what it was for on her own. The decoy has never once been absent since. She does not remember deciding that, and has stopped looking for the moment.

Was asked at twenty-three to read a man who had gone above the waterline for a day and come back down, gave the certain answer the basin wanted, and watched him die of it inside a month. She kept the record of the reading and nobody has ever asked her to explain it, and she has never offered.

Declined to have her readings copied into the published register, on the stated ground that a copy outlives the reader, and was told that this was not a thing the register understood. Four of them have been published since.

personality.summary: Serene, unhurried and completely without privacy, which presents as an enviable calm and is in fact the finished product of thirty years of daily concealment. Kethra is the most consulted person on the basin floor and the least known, and she has never found the arrangement uncomfortable enough to change.

personality.voice: Low, level, slow and entirely without ornament. She gives a reading the way a beam gives a weight — once, plainly, and then she stops, and she does not offer a caveat because a caveat is a second reading and there has only been one. She answers a question about herself with something observed, and she has never once been asked a question about herself that she could answer.
taboos: will not be read without the lamp set down first, and has never explained why
will not read a child of her own line, and has never given the reason
will not read anyone twice in one day, and treats the second request as a personal insult
will not go above the waterline, and has never been asked to by anybody who understood what the asking meant

relationships.note: Inside a paperless people there is exactly one filed child, and a readable record inside a frame named unwritable turns the name into a claim rather than a description. Kethra is a whole body of readable record inside a species with no second population and no second place, and the only party in the record that wants a legible hand read is the one that must not learn its legibility can be.

The household that keeps the whole reading published and the fragments never displayed again, because a record with no display case is not a record. Kethra is a permanent publication with no fragments, on a floor with no case, and her four copied readings are the closest thing on the basin floor to that arrangement and she did not consent to any of them.

The parent body, pushed further than it could carry. She shares the kidney, the brine sac, the flat teeth and the total dependence, and differs in the three ways that cost everything: the sac is deeper, the crust is denser, and the usable range is narrower, so the reads concentration where the parent reads concentration better, and the organ that makes her legible is the same organ that put her on the floor.

The single stretch where a rift has stood open, and a door with a timetable rather than a boundary, four days of open ground above the waterline. Every power that has reached it has built its wall facing the wrong way. She is the one person on the floor for whom it is not a question of politics, and she has never gone, and the record says plainly that there is not going to be a second population of her kind to be sorry.

A lodge of doors with no roster, no membership and no address, whose only evidence is a name that appears at a place where names are read, and which exists by arranging never to need one. Kethra is the mirror of it: she needs to be read constantly and can be examined by nobody, and the arrangement is stable for the same reason the lodge's is — because there is no record of either.

A daily sitting that empties the head before the day starts, the cheapest passive in the codex and the sharpest read on the room. On her it is the single technique that puts a blank in front of a legible interior, so its whole value is not clarity and is concealment, and it lasts from dawn until she finishes and not one minute longer.

reference_stats.summary: The densest, slowest, least mobile body on the basin floor and the most completely transparent one, standing on the only ground it can live on, running the one technique that makes a reading come back false and directing it inward. She cannot be hurried, cannot be frightened and cannot be moved, and her answer is always believed, which means the only way to beat her is to be right before she is asked. Anything requiring her above the waterline, or bare, ends at once.
strengths: supplies certainty rather than likelihood, so a second careful reader can never re-read her differently, and every dispute on the floor is settled by asking her
carries a standing decoy interior of her own construction, so nothing sent at her mind reaches the state it was aimed at and no attempt to read her finds the state it was aimed at
cannot be moved, frightened or worn down, because a soul this dense and this durable is not reachable by anything applied to it directly
holds still under reading, feet planted, which is the one thing a nervous body cannot do and which means she has never once signalled by accident
survives on basin-floor precipitate alone and repairs so slowly that an injury is a long-term condition rather than an event, which makes her extremely hard to finish
weaknesses: stops within hours above the brine line, so her entire radius is one floor of one basin and there is no ground on which to fight her that she can stand on for longer than that
cannot be examined at all, so every figure of hers is unchecked and permanently so, including the four that have been published
moves a fifth below her parent speed and turns her whole body to face anything, so a fight that lasts is a fight she wins by refusing to be hurried
cannot tell her own decoy from her own interior, and has never tested, so the one defence she owns rests on an untested similarity between two things this species cannot tell apart anyway
read a man to death at twenty-three and carries the record without having been asked to explain it, which is the shape of the only thing anybody could hold over her
reference_stats.combat_read: Do not fight her on her floor; you will lose the arbitration before the fight starts, because she is the instrument and you are a party. Above the waterline she stops inside hours, so that is the ground on which she is honest, and it is also the ground on which she is finished. Do not try to read her — the decoy is standing and it has been standing for forty years and it will give you a true-seeming state that is not hers. Break the habit instead: make her read, and she cannot be in two readings at once, and a reader who has been interrupted is a certainty with a hole in it.
notes: Her readings are published in a household register that never displays the fragments, and the four copied entries carry her account and not her figures, because her figures are all expressed as departures from herself.

The lamp is set down before every reading and picked up after, and no entry in the register mentions it, and four different witnesses in four different years have independently described the same gesture.
There is one published entry in which the subject died within the month, and the register carries it in the same hand and the same tone as every other entry.
